question_text: If 3sinθ + 4cosθ = 5, then find the value of 4sinθ − 3cosθ.

mark_split.label: Name the unknown and square both

steps.label: Name the unknown and square both
steps.margin_note: First mark. Same method as the general case: call the wanted value x and square and add.

recall.must_convey: That the wanted expression is named x and both are squared and added.

name the unknown x and square and add the two
use the squaring and adding method
x ani peru petti square chesi add cheyyali
square both expressions and add them

steps.why: The coefficients are swapped and one sign flipped between the two expressions, which is exactly the pattern that makes squaring and adding work.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to square the 5 on the right.

steps.label: Expand, cancel and solve
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The 24 sinθ cosθ terms cancel, leaving 25(sin²θ + cos²θ) = 25 — so x² = 0 and x can only be 0.
steps.memory_tip: The 24 sinθcosθ terms cancel, leaving 25 — so x² = 0 and x can only be 0.

recall.must_convey: That the cross terms cancel to leave 25, so x² = 0 and x = 0.
accept: the twenty four terms cancel leaving twenty five so x squared is zero and x is zero
x squared plus twenty five equals twenty five so x is zero
cross terms cancel ayi twenty five vasthundi, x zero
four sin theta minus three cos theta is zero

steps.why: x² = 0 has only ONE root, so unlike the general case there is no ± here — zero is its own negative.
common_mistakes: Concluding x = 5 by misreading the equation.

insider_note: Name the wanted expression x, then SQUARE AND ADD — the cross terms cancel and everything collapses to 25. x² = 0 means the answer is exactly 0, not ± something.
